newsitem.title: USA: Oilseed exports still at risk due Egypt ban-USDA.
newsitem.headline: Oilseed exports still at risk due Egypt ban-USDA.

text.p: A senior U.S. Agriculture Department official Friday said Egypt's new import ban on genetically-altered commodities had been put on hold for three months "for everything but oilseeds."

"There is still quite a lot of confusion about what the Egyptian government intends to do," said Paul Drazek, trade adviser to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman. "We're still working the issue very very hard through our embassy."
"I still remain optimistic we can solve it in short order," he added.

Last week, the news came out that the Egyptian Health Ministry had unexpectedly issued a decree, dated July 1, that it would require imports of commodities meant for human consumption be accompanied by proof that genetic engineering was not used in their production.
About 15 percent of the soybeans U.S. farmers will harvest this year will come from genetically-altered plants.
